text:
anya: Quick sync — proposing a focused experiment to cut long-term storage and tail query cost by doing aggressive rollups for traces older than 7d. Idea: keep full spans for 7d, 30d keep a compact per-request rollup + 0.5-1% sampled spans for debugging, 90d metrics-only rollups. Short thread with tradeoffs and runbook.
liam: Sounds interesting. Main worry is long-tail debugging — we'll lose span-level search for old incidents. How do we decide which traces keep full fidelity?
morgan: We can preserve full spans for traces that meet a fast heuristic: error_count>0 OR latency_p99 > 1s OR flagged by a customer alert. That keeps the important ones.
dmitri: How expensive is that heuristic at ingest? We can't add heavy lookups before write path.
anya: Plan is lightweight: compute a tiny "trace_score" at ingest from existing fields (error boolean, duration ms, sampling_hint header). This is O(1) per trace and just a few ops. If score >= threshold we write full spans to cold tier; otherwise route to rollup pipeline.
liam: Can you paste the retention tiers we want to pilot? numbers help.
anya: sure — quick snippet:
```
7d  -> full spans + full index
30d -> rollup: per-request summary (counts, top N ops, agg timings) + sampled spans (~0.5%)
90d -> metrics-only rollup (per-route aggregates, error rates)
```
liam: OK. What about query UX? Developers will try `find-span by request_id` and come up empty for older traces.
morgan: UX mitigation: 1) return a clear message when full trace not available and link to rollup view, 2) keep a lightweight trace breadcrumb index (request_id -> rollup_id and tenant_id) for 180d. That allows basic lookup and quick escalation to retained full traces if needed.
dmitri: Breadcrumb index size? If we store just (tenant_id, request_hash, timestamp, rollup_id) that's ~32 bytes per trace. At 100M traces/mo that's ~3.2GB/mo — acceptable in cold index.
liam: Also need billing and cost attribution mapping. Rollups must keep tenant/shard metadata so we can attribute storage/query cost back to customer.
anya: Agreed — rollup proto will include tenant_id, billing_key, and a small token for query stitching. No PII in rollup.
morgan: Edge case: customer runs ad-hoc debug requiring full traces older than 30d. What's the escalation path?
anya: Runbook: support can request a cold restore of the full spans (from short-term backups) — expected RTO 2-6 hours for single trace retrieval. We add a self-serve drawer later if this proves high-frequency.
dmitri: We should add a safety net: any trace that triggered an incident or belongs to an active SLA window (last 30 days before an SLO breach) auto-retains full spans for 90d.
anya: Good call. We'll add an SLO-preserve flag in ingest scoring + post-facto retention extension from alert hooks.
liam: Metrics to collect for the 2-week pilot: storage delta (GB), query latency at 95/99 for trace searches, fraction of trace lookups that hit rollup (vs retained full), and number of restore requests.
morgan: Also capture developer satisfaction: quick poll after pilot and whether the rollup view answers 80% of investigations.
anya: I'll create the experiment ticket and config. Experiment name: infra/rollup-retention-experiment-369988. Pilot scope: staging + subset prod (5% traffic) for 2 weeks. Success criteria: >=30% storage reduction on cold tier and <=10% increase in mean query latency for trace search.
liam: :thumbsup: please add a kill-switch and circuit breaker that disables rollups if restore requests spike or if SLOs degrade.
dmitri: I'll add metrics and alerting for restore rate and rollup-induced query errors.
sre-bot: Experiment created: infra/rollup-retention-experiment-369988. Dashboards: infra.storage.rollup, obs.query.latency.rollup, obs.restore.rate. Monitors attached.
anya: Thanks everyone. I'll post the experiment config and the ingest scoring pseudo-code in the experiment ticket shortly. We'll reconvene after 48h of data.
